Stir in crushed tomatoes and red pepper flakes (if using). Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cook for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
In a separate saucepan, melt butter. Whisk in flour to form a roux. Cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in milk until smooth and thickened, about 3-4 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
In a large bowl, whisk eggs. Slowly whisk in a ladleful of the hot milk mixture to temper the eggs. Add the tempered egg mixture back into the remaining milk mixture. Stir well.
Combine cooked macaroni, sausage-mushroom-tomato mixture, milk sauce, shredded mozzarella, and 25g Parmesan in the large bowl. Mix thoroughly.
Pour mixture into the prepared baking dish.
In a small bowl, combine panko breadcrumbs and remaining 25g Parmesan. Sprinkle evenly over the top of the macaroni mixture.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until bubbling and the topping is golden brown.
Let rest for 5 minutes before serving. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: For a spicier dish, use hot Italian sausage and increase red pepper flakes.
Leftovers can be stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Cacciatore
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of rustic chicken cacciatore served in a shallow, cream-colored ceramic bowl with minor surface imperfections. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs are the centerpiece, their skin appearing dark golden and tender from braising. The chicken is partially submerged in a thick, chunky tomato sauce featuring visible pieces of softened translucent onions and whole black olives. A single fresh rosemary sprig is placed casually on top. The bowl sits on a weathered dark wood kitchen table. Beside the bowl is a thick piece of torn crusty bread. The scene is illuminated by warm, soft overhead kitchen lighting, creating a cozy, authentic Italian home-dining atmosphere. A simple linen napkin and a stainless steel fork are placed to the left of the bowl.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty sourdough bread to soak up the tomato sauce
Pair with a side of simple polenta or rustic mashed potatoes
Traditional family-style dining involves placing the skillet in the center of the table
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper on all sides.
Heat olive oil in a large deep skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down for 6 minutes until golden brown.
Flip chicken and sear for 4 minutes. Remove chicken from skillet.
Add diced onion to the skillet. Sauté for 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add crushed tomatoes, oregano, and the rosemary sprig.
Place chicken back into the skillet, nestled into the sauce.
Simmer on low heat for 30 minutes until chicken reaches 75°C internally.
Stir in the olives 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Use bone-in thighs for maximum flavor and protein content
Ensure the sauce reduces until thick to concentrate the savory tomato profile
Always check the thickest part of the chicken for a safe internal temperature of 75°C

recipes.recipe_name: Mushroom, Green Bean & Pear Salad
recipes.visual_description: The Mushroom, Green Bean & Pear Salad is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. A vibrant bed of fresh mixed salad greens forms the base. Roasted mushrooms, halved or quartered and golden-brown, are scattered artfully, providing an earthy contrast. Crisp-tender green beans, cut into 3 cm pieces, intermingle with bright green peas, adding varied verdant hues. Diced pear cubes, with creamy white flesh, and halved red grapes, showcasing deep ruby tones, are interspersed, contributing sweet, juicy notes. The composition is lightly coated with a glistening vinaigrette. A sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped parsley adds a final vibrant green touch. The plate rests on a simple wooden table, with a cotton napkin, under natural, even lighting, creating a casual bistro ambiance.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Halve or quarter mushrooms. Toss with 1 tbsp olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast for 15-20 minutes until tender and browned.
Bring a pot of salted water to a boil. Blanch green beans for 2-3 minutes until crisp-tender. Immediately transfer to an ice bath. Drain well. Cut beans into 3 cm pieces.
Blanch green peas in the same boiling water for 1 minute. Drain and refresh in cold water.
Core and dice the pear into 1.5 cm cubes. Halve the red grapes.
In a small bowl, whisk together remaining olive oil, white balsamic vinegar, Dijon mustard, honey (if using), salt, and pepper for the dressing.
In a large bowl, combine roasted mushrooms, blanched green beans, green peas, diced pear, and halved grapes.
Add mixed salad greens to the bowl. Pour dressing over the salad ingredients. Toss gently to combine.
Divide the salad among four plates. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley or chives.

recipes.recipe_name: Poulet Suprême, Tomate Confite et Jus Ailé
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly pan-seared chicken supreme, skin crisp and golden-brown, rests elegantly on a pristine white bone china plate with a subtle, organic rim. The chicken, presented whole, dominates the left side of the plate, its natural form preserved. A glistening, dark amber chicken jus, infused with garlic and tomato essence, forms an organic, flowing pool beneath and around the chicken, reflecting light. To the right, a small, vibrant cluster of burst and softened confit cherry tomatoes, their skins gently wrinkled, adds a pop of rich red and orange. Beside the tomatoes, a small, artfully sculpted quenelle of creamy, pale beige garlic purée provides a soft textural contrast. A single, delicate sprig of fresh chervil or tarragon is precisely placed on the chicken or jus, offering a touch of verdant green and aromatic freshness. Abundant negative space surrounds the components, emphasizing the minimalist and architectural precision of the plating. The plate sits on a premium grey veined marble surface, accompanied by a single, precisely folded white linen napkin and polished silver flatware. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, highlighting the textures and rich colors of the dish against an ultra-minimalist background, creating a scene of sophisticated culinary artistry.
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C.

For Confit Tomatoes and Garlic: Place cherry tomatoes and 8 unpeeled garlic cloves in a small baking dish. Drizzle with 30ml olive oil. Add 2 thyme sprigs. Season lightly with salt. Roast for 45-60 minutes, until tomatoes burst and garlic is soft. Peel garlic cloves after roasting.

For Garlic Purée: Peel 4 raw garlic cloves. Blanch in boiling water for 1 minute. Drain. Repeat blanching twice more. Combine blanched garlic with 2 roasted confit garlic cloves and 10g butter. Mash to a smooth purée. Season with salt.

For Chicken Jus Ailé: Finely dice shallots. In a saucepan, heat 10ml olive oil. Sauté shallots until translucent. Add 2 roasted confit garlic cloves and 2 thyme sprigs. Deglaze with white wine; reduce by half. Add chicken stock. Simmer gently for 20 minutes, reducing liquid by half. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve. Discard solids. Return liquid to pan. Whisk in 20g cold butter. Keep warm.

For Chicken Suprêmes: Pat chicken supremes dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Heat remaining 10ml olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken skin-side down. Sear for 6-8 minutes until skin is deeply golden and crispy. Flip chicken. Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Roast for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Let rest 5 minutes before plating.

To Serve: Spoon a natural pool of chicken jus onto each plate. Place one rested chicken supreme on top. Arrange a small cluster of confit cherry tomatoes beside the chicken. Add a small, elegant quenelle of garlic purée. Garnish with a small sprig of fresh chervil or tarragon.

recipes.recipe_name: Black Bean and Rice Salad with Chicken
recipes.visual_description: A hearty Black Bean and Rice Salad is presented in a wide, shallow ceramic bowl, characteristic of home kitchenware. The components are naturally arranged, with a generous portion filling the bowl. Diced chicken cubes are interspersed among the fluffy, cooled white rice and dark, glossy black beans. Bright green peas and flecks of finely diced red chili add pops of color. Chopped fresh basil leaves are scattered throughout, providing an aromatic garnish. The ingredients are lightly coated in a simple, clear dressing, giving them a slight sheen. The salad appears fresh and wholesome. The bowl sits on a well-used, light-colored wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, natural kitchen light. A simple cloth napkin and everyday flatware are casually placed beside the bowl, suggesting a relaxed family meal.

ingredients.name: Canned black beans, rinsed and drained
Red chili, deseeded and finely diced

instructions: Cook chicken breast until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Dice chicken into 1.5 cm cubes. Set aside to cool.
Ensure cooked rice is completely cooled. Fluff with a fork.
Rinse and drain canned black beans thoroughly.
Thaw frozen green peas. Optionally, blanch quickly for brighter color, then cool.
Finely dice the deseeded red chili. Chop fresh basil leaves.
Prepare the dressing: In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, lime juice, honey, ground cumin (if using), salt, and black pepper.
In a large mixing bowl, combine the diced chicken, cooled rice, black beans, green peas, diced chili, and chopped basil.
Pour the dressing over the salad ingredients. Toss gently to coat everything evenly.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed. Serve chilled or at room temperature.

recipes.recipe_name: Jasmine Tea Broth with Chocolate Coconut Bua Loy
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a minimalist, premium beige travertine sharing platter, featuring several small, pristine white bone china bowls. Each bowl holds 4-5 perfectly spherical, glistening white glutinous rice dumplings, gently floating in a clear, pale golden jasmine tea broth. The dumplings are plump and smooth, hinting at the rich chocolate-coconut core within. A delicate scattering of tiny, golden-brown crispy sago pearls adorns the surface of the broth, providing a textural counterpoint and subtle shimmer. The composition is clean and architectural, with abundant negative space on the platter, emphasizing the purity of ingredients and precision of execution. A pristine white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, rests beside the bowls. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, enhancing the refined simplicity and elegance of the presentation, evoking a tranquil, sophisticated Thai culinary experience.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve communally on a sharing platter.
Offer small porcelain spoons for the broth and dumplings.
instructions: Prepare Ganache Core:
Heat cream in a small saucepan until simmering. Do not boil.
Pour hot cream over chopped milk chocolate in a heatproof bowl. Let sit 1 minute.
Whisk gently from center outwards until smooth.
Stir in coconut liqueur and cold butter until fully incorporated and ganache is glossy.
Transfer ganache to a piping bag or small bowl. Chill 1-2 hours until firm enough to handle.
Roll ganache into small spheres, about 1 cm diameter. Place on parchment-lined tray. Freeze 30 minutes.
Prepare Dumpling Dough:
In a large bowl, combine glutinous rice flour.
Gradually add warm water, kneading until a smooth, pliable, non-sticky dough forms. Adjust water as needed.
Divide dough into 16-20 equal portions.
Assemble Dumplings:
Flatten each dough portion into a small disc.
Place one frozen ganache sphere in the center of each disc.
Carefully wrap dough around ganache, sealing completely. Roll into a smooth sphere.
Place finished dumplings on a lightly floured surface.
Cook Crispy Sago:
Heat vegetable oil in a small saucepan to 170°C.
Add sago pearls in small batches. Fry until puffed and golden brown, about 1-2 minutes.
Remove with a slotted spoon. Drain on paper towels. Season lightly with a pinch of sugar, if desired.
Prepare Jasmine Tea Broth:
Bring water to a boil in a saucepan. Remove from heat.
Add jasmine tea leaves. Steep 5 minutes.
Strain tea, discarding leaves. Return liquid to saucepan.
Stir in caster sugar until dissolved. Keep warm over low heat.
Cook Dumplings:
Bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil.
Carefully drop dumplings into boiling water.
Cook until dumplings float to the surface and puff slightly, about 3-5 minutes.
Remove cooked dumplings with a slotted spoon. Briefly immerse in an ice bath to prevent sticking and maintain shape.
Final Assembly and Serve:
Place 4-5 cooked dumplings in each serving bowl.
Ladle warm jasmine tea broth over dumplings.
Garnish sparingly with crispy sago pearls.
Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure ganache spheres are well-frozen for easy encasing.
Do not overcrowd the pot when cooking dumplings.
Crispy sago should be fried quickly to prevent burning.
Adjust sugar in broth to desired sweetness.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef Cheek, Refined Sauerkraut, Mustard Seed Gastrique
recipes.visual_description: A single, generously portioned, glistening mahogany braised beef cheek rests centrally on a pristine white bone china plate with a subtle, elegant rim. The beef, incredibly tender, shows its natural, irregular shape, not sliced. Adjacent to it, a small, artfully shaped quenelle of pale green, refined sauerkraut provides a delicate contrast, its finely shredded texture visible. A rich, dark, glossy reduction sauce is drizzled thoughtfully over the beef and around its base. Precise dots and a fine drizzle of golden-amber mustard seed gastrique are strategically placed, adding vibrant color and textural intrigue from the visible mustard seeds. The plate is largely negative space, emphasizing the clean, minimalist composition. The setting features a luxurious grey-veined marble surface, a folded white linen napkin, and a single piece of polished silver flatware, all under dramatic professional lighting that creates subtle, soft shadows and highlights the dish's refined elegance.
instructions: Trim beef cheeks of excess fat and sinew. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a heavy-bottomed Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear beef cheeks on all sides until deeply browned. Remove beef and set aside.
Add carrot, onion, and celery to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 8 minutes. Add garlic and tomato paste; cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Deglaze with red wine, scraping up any browned bits. Reduce by half, about 5 minutes.
Return beef cheeks to the pot. Add beef stock, thyme, and bay leaves. Bring to a simmer. Cover and transfer to a preheated oven at 150°C for 3-4 hours, or until beef is fork-tender.

Remove beef cheeks from the pot. Strain the braising liquid through a fine-mesh sieve, discarding solids. Return liquid to the pot and reduce over medium-high heat until it forms a rich, glossy sauce. Season with salt and pepper. Keep beef warm in a small amount of sauce.
Rinse sauerkraut under cold water for 1 minute to reduce acidity. Drain very well, squeezing out excess liquid.

Melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Add finely diced apple and sauté for 3 minutes. Add the rinsed sauerkraut and white wine. Cook gently, stirring occasionally, for 15-20 minutes, until sauerkraut is tender and mellow. Season with salt.

For the mustard seed gastrique: In a small saucepan, melt sugar over medium heat until it caramelizes to an amber color. Do not stir. Carefully deglaze with red wine vinegar; it will bubble vigorously. Add yellow mustard seeds and Dijon mustard. Simmer for 3-5 minutes until slightly thickened. If too thick, add a touch of water or braising liquid. Season with a pinch of salt.

To plate: Place a single braised beef cheek centrally on each plate. Arrange a small, elegant quenelle or neat mound of the refined sauerkraut beside the beef. Drizzle the reduced braising sauce over and around the beef. Artistically dot or drizzle the mustard seed gastrique around the plate.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo en Salsa Verde con Chile de Arbol
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pollo en Salsa Verde is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A generous, whole seared chicken thigh, its surface golden-brown from searing, is nestled within a vibrant, glossy green salsa. The sauce, rich and emulsified, pools around the chicken, flecked with tiny dark specks from the roasted arbol chiles. A light scattering of freshly chopped coriander leaves provides a bright green garnish and aromatic contrast. The plate is set on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a small, authentic Mexican ceramic bowl holding fluffy white rice and a stack of warm corn tortillas wrapped in a cloth. A simple cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and vibrant color. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space, creating a professional yet inviting presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas.
Serve with traditional Mexican rice.
Serve with refried beans on the side.
Offer a small dish of pickled red onions or jalapeños.
instructions: Heat a dry comal or heavy skillet over medium-high heat. Add tomatillos, arbol chiles, half the onion, and garlic cloves.

Roast ingredients, turning occasionally, until tomatillos soften and char slightly (10-12 minutes). Chiles and garlic toast faster (2-3 minutes). Remove chiles and garlic when fragrant and lightly browned to prevent burning.
Transfer roasted tomatillos, chiles, garlic, and onion to a blender. Add fresh coriander, chicken broth, and a pinch of salt. Blend until smooth.
Season chicken thighs with salt. Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add chicken thighs to the hot oil. Sear for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Cook to an internal temperature of 75°C.
Pour the blended salsa verde over the seared chicken. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 15-20 minutes, allowing chicken to absorb flavors.
Check seasoning. Add a pinch of sugar if the sauce is too acidic.
Serve hot.
notes: Adjust the number of arbol chiles to your preferred spice level.
For a thicker sauce, simmer uncovered for an additional 5-10 minutes.

recipes.recipe_name: South Indian Chicken Fry with Cashews
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of South Indian Chicken Fry is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Succulent, golden-brown chicken chunks are coated in a rich, semi-dry, reddish-brown masala. Whole and halved raw cashews are visibly mixed throughout, adding textural contrast. Fresh, vibrant green coriander leaves are scattered over the top as garnish. Chicken pieces are piled neatly in the center, avoiding fanned arrangements, with moderate negative space. A small white ceramic bowl of fluffy basmati rice and a lime wedge sit beside the main dish. The setting is a modern bistro with a simple wooden table and a cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene. The background is minimal, showcasing a casual restaurant ambiance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with basmati rice
Serve with warm naan bread or paratha
Accompanied by a side of raita or simple cucumber salad
instructions: Heat coconut oil in a large pan over medium heat.
Add curry leaves and slit green chilies. Sauté 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add sliced red onion. Sauté 5-7 minutes until soft and light golden.
Add minced garlic and grated ginger. Sauté 1 minute until aromatic.
Add turmeric powder, red chili powder, coriander powder, and garam masala. Stir 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add chopped tomato. Cook 3-4 minutes, pressing with spoon, until soft and oil separates.
Add chicken chunks and salt. Stir to coat chicken evenly with masala.
Pour in 100 ml water. Bring to a simmer. Cover pan. Cook 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until chicken is tender and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Remove lid. Increase heat to medium-high. Cook 5-7 minutes, stirring frequently, until liquid reduces and masala coats chicken well. The dish should be semi-dry.
Add cashews. Stir 2 minutes until lightly toasted and integrated.
Stir in fresh chopped coriander leaves.
Serve hot.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Adjust green chilies and red chili powder to control spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Chicken & Fermented Vegetable Bowl
recipes.visual_description: A refined, individual portion of Sustainable Chicken & Fermented Vegetable Bowl in a handcrafted, earthy-toned ceramic bowl. Fluffy brown rice forms the base. A beautifully seared chicken thigh, with crispy golden skin, is placed prominently. Roasted broccoli florets, caramelized onion wedges, and halved cremini mushrooms are artfully arranged around the chicken, showcasing natural colors and textures. A vibrant, quick-lacto-fermented carrot pickle, cut into thin rounds, adds a bright pop of orange and a distinct preserved element. The composition is minimalistic, with ample white space, emphasizing purity and natural beauty. Garnish with fresh parsley or dill. The bowl sits on a light, natural wood surface, complemented by an undyed linen napkin. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish, highlighting organic textures. The background is clean and unobtrusive, with a hint of natural greenery, reinforcing the eco-conscious theme.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a complete meal, highlighting the balance of protein, grains, and fermented elements.
Encourage mindful eating, appreciating each ingredient's contribution to a sustainable diet.
instructions: Prepare Fermented Carrot Pickle: Wash and thinly slice carrots into rounds or batons. Dissolve 10g non-chlorinated salt in 500ml water to make brine. Pack carrots tightly into a clean jar. Pour brine over carrots, ensuring they are fully submerged. Cover loosely or use an airlock. Let ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days, or until desired tanginess is achieved. Refrigerate after fermentation.

Prepare Chicken: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until golden brown and crispy, about 8-10 minutes. Flip and sear for another 2-3 minutes. Remove skillet from heat. Transfer chicken to a plate. Drain excess fat, reserving about 15ml in the pan.

Cook Rice: Rinse brown rice thoroughly. Combine rice with 500ml water and a pinch of salt in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 40-45 minutes, or until water is absorbed and rice is tender. Let stand, covered, for 10 minutes, then fluff with a fork.

Roast Vegetables: Preheat oven to 200°C. Roughly chop broccoli into florets. Halve cremini mushrooms. Peel and cut onion into wedges. Peel and smash garlic cloves. Toss all vegetables with remaining olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet. Roast for 20-25 minutes, until tender and slightly caramelized.

Finish Chicken: Place chicken thighs skin-side up back into the skillet (or a new baking dish). Bake in the preheated oven with the vegetables for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Let chicken rest for 5 minutes before serving.

Assemble Bowls: Divide cooked brown rice among 4 bowls. Place one chicken thigh on top of or next to the rice in each bowl. Arrange roasted vegetables around the chicken and rice. Add a generous portion of fermented carrot pickle to each bowl. Garnish with fresh parsley or dill.
notes: For zero-waste, chicken bones and vegetable scraps can be simmered with water to create a light broth for future use.
The fermented carrot pickle can be prepared days in advance, enhancing its probiotic benefits and flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Aromatic Fish and Rice Pilaf
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Aromatic Fish and Rice Pilaf is presented in a simple, deep ceramic bowl with a slightly rustic texture. The fluffy basmati rice, gently tinted golden from turmeric, is mixed with tender, opaque white chunks of flaked white fish, approximately 4cm pieces. Soft, translucent onion and diced tomato pieces are visible throughout, along with vibrant green fresh cilantro leaves generously scattered on top. The pilaf is naturally mounded, creating a comforting, unpretentious look. The bowl rests on a well-worn, light-colored wooden dining table. A simple, folded linen napkin and a traditional metal serving spoon are casually placed nearby. Warm, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, evoking a homely kitchen atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with plain yogurt or a simple cucumber raita (yogurt mixed with grated cucumber and a pinch of salt).
instructions: Rinse basmati rice. Soak 20 minutes. Drain well.
Cut fish into 4 cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Chop onion finely. Mince garlic and ginger. Dice tomatoes.
Heat oil in large pot or deep pan over medium heat.
Add cumin seeds. Sauté until fragrant.
Add chopped onion. Cook until translucent.
Add minced garlic and ginger. Sauté 1 minute.
Add diced tomatoes. Cook until softened.
Add coriander powder, turmeric powder, salt, and pepper. Stir 30 seconds.
Add drained basmati rice. Stir gently 2 minutes to coat.
Pour in 600 ml water. Bring to a boil.
Gently place fish chunks on top of rice. Do not stir.
Reduce heat to low. Cover tightly. Cook 15-18 minutes until water absorbed and rice tender.
Remove from heat. Let stand, covered, 10 minutes.
Fluff rice gently with fork. Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro.
traditional_techniques: Dum cooking (steaming in a sealed pot)

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Indian Butter Chicken with Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Creamy Indian Butter Chicken with Potatoes is presented in a deep, pristine white ceramic bowl. The rich, vibrant orange-red curry fills the bowl, exhibiting a smooth, velvety texture. Tender, golden-brown seared chicken chunks are nestled within the sauce. Quartered roasted potatoes, with slightly browned edges, are partially submerged, adding visual weight and texture. A delicate swirl of fresh cream adorns the top, complemented by a generous sprinkle of bright green, finely chopped fresh cilantro leaves. The dish is placed on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. Beside the bowl, a white porcelain dinner plate awaits, ready for basmati rice or naan. Small, polished stainless steel Katori bowls, holding potential accompaniments like raita or pickled onions, complete the authentic Indian dining setup. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's inviting colors and textures, creating a professional yet approachable presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with fluffy basmati rice or warm naan bread.
Offer a side of cooling raita (yogurt with cucumber and spices) or pickled onions.
Enjoy family-style, allowing diners to scoop curry onto their rice or bread.

ingredients.name: Cashews, soaked in hot water for 15 minutes

instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 4 cm chunks. Season with salt and 1 teaspoon Kashmiri chili powder. Set aside.

Heat half the butter/ghee in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken chunks in batches until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken and set aside. Cook to internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Reduce heat to medium. Add remaining butter/ghee. Add bay leaf, cinnamon stick, cardamom pods, and cloves. Sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add chopped onion. Cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in ginger-garlic paste. Cook for 1 minute until aromatic.
Add remaining Kashmiri chili powder, cumin, coriander, and turmeric. Cook for 30 seconds, stirring constantly.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Bring to a simmer. Add soaked cashews. Cook for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens and oil separates.

Remove whole spices (bay leaf, cinnamon, cardamom, cloves). Carefully transfer sauce to a blender. Blend until completely smooth. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pot for a silkier sauce (optional).
Return seared chicken to the pot with the smooth sauce. Add quartered potatoes. Stir to combine.
Add 150 millilitres of water. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cover and cook for 20-25 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through and potatoes are tender. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
Stir in heavy cream, crushed fenugreek leaves, salt, and sugar (if using). Simmer for 5 minutes, uncovered, until sauce reaches desired consistency.
Remove from heat. Discard any remaining whole spices if desired. Garnish generously with fresh chopped cilantro before serving.
notes: For best flavor, marinate chicken for at least 30 minutes, or up to 4 hours in the refrigerator.
Adjust the amount of Kashmiri chili powder to control the color and mild heat.
Soaking cashews helps achieve a smoother sauce.

recipes.recipe_name: Brasato di Manzo con Polenta Cremosa e Zucca Arrosto
recipes.visual_description: The dish is centrally presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. A generous, free-flowing mound of creamy, golden polenta forms the base. Nestled atop are two to three substantial, irregularly shaped chunks of rich, dark brown braised beef, glistening from its deep red-brown tomato and red wine sauce which pools slightly. Alongside, a vibrant scattering of roasted butternut squash cubes, lightly caramelized and golden-orange, and bright yellow corn kernels adds color and varied texture. A light dusting of finely grated pale yellow Parmesan cheese and fresh, finely chopped green parsley provides a fresh accent. The setting is a modern bistro, with a simple light wooden table. A folded cotton napkin sits beside the plate. Natural, soft lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the food's rich colors and textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a glass of robust red wine, such as Chianti or Barolo.
Offer crusty bread for soaking up the rich sauce.
Enjoy as a hearty main course during colder months.

ingredients.name: Butternut Squash
ingredients.quantity: 800 g, peeled, deseeded, cut into 2 cm cubes

instructions: Pat beef chunks dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. Sear beef chunks on all sides until deeply browned. Remove beef and set aside.
Add diced onion, carrots, and celery to the pot. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 8-10 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze the pot with red wine, scraping up any browned bits. Bring to a simmer and cook for 2 minutes.
Return beef to the pot. Add diced tomatoes, beef broth, rosemary, thyme, and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and braise for 2.5-3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender. Stir occasionally.

While beef braises, preheat oven to 200°C. Toss butternut squash cubes with a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet. Roast for 20-25 minutes, or until tender and lightly caramelized. Add corn kernels to the baking sheet for the last 10 minutes of roasting.
Prepare polenta: Bring water or vegetable broth to a boil in a medium saucepan. Slowly whisk in cornmeal, stirring constantly to prevent lumps.
Reduce heat to low. Cook polenta, stirring frequently, for 20-25 minutes, until thick and creamy. Add more liquid if needed.
Stir butter and 40 g of Parmesan cheese into the polenta. Season with salt.
Remove braised beef from sauce. Shred or cut into large chunks. Skim any excess fat from the sauce. Remove herbs and bay leaf.
Serve braised beef chunks over creamy polenta. Spoon roasted squash and corn alongside. Garnish with remaining grated Parmesan and fresh chopped parsley.
notes: For deeper flavor, braise the beef a day ahead and gently reheat. The flavors meld beautifully overnight.
Adjust sauce consistency by simmering longer for a thicker sauce, or adding more broth if too thick.

recipes.recipe_name: Beet Risotto with Seared Scallops
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant, creamy beet risotto forms the base, presented as a free-flowing, rich magenta pool on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The risotto is cooked to a fluid, al dente consistency, with visible rice grains suspended within the smooth, earthy beet purée. Four perfectly seared sea scallops, each with a beautiful golden-brown crust and opaque, tender centers, are arranged artfully atop the risotto. The scallops are whole, plump, and not sliced. A scattering of bright green, finely chopped fresh parsley provides a striking color contrast against the deep red risotto and golden scallops. The dish is centrally placed on a simple wooden table surface. A white cotton napkin and classic silver flatware are neatly arranged beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's textures and colors, creating an inviting, casual bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty bread.
Pair with a crisp, dry white wine like Pinot Grigio or Sauvignon Blanc.
Finish the meal with espresso.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Roast whole beets until tender, about 45-60 minutes. Peel roasted beets. Puree beets in a blender with a splash of broth until smooth. Set aside.
Warm broth in a saucepan. Keep it simmering gently.
Finely dice shallot and mince garlic.
In a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven, heat 15 ml olive oil over medium heat. Add diced shallot. Cook until translucent, about 3-4 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice to the pot. Stir constantly for 2 minutes until edges of grains are translucent.
Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed.

Add a ladleful of warm broth to the rice. Stir constantly until absorbed. Stir in the beet puree. Continue adding broth, one ladleful at a time, stirring frequently until each addition is absorbed before adding more. This takes about 18-20 minutes. The risotto should be creamy and al dente.
Remove risotto from heat. Stir in cold, cubed butter and grated Parmesan cheese. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Cover. Let rest 2 minutes.
While risotto rests, prepare scallops. Pat scallops very dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat remaining 15 ml olive oil in a large non-stick pan over high heat until shimmering. Place scallops in a single layer, ensuring not to overcrowd the pan. Sear undisturbed for 2-3 minutes until a deep golden-brown crust forms. Flip scallops. Sear for another 1-2 minutes until cooked through and opaque. Cook scallops to an internal temperature of 63°C (145°F).
Spoon a generous portion of beet risotto onto each plate. Arrange 4 seared scallops on top of the risotto.
Finely chop fresh parsley or chives. Sprinkle over scallops and risotto. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure scallops are very dry before searing for best crust.
Adjust broth quantity for desired risotto consistency.

recipes.recipe_name: Cubi di Formaggio Dolce con Mela e Malto
recipes.visual_description: Eight perfectly uniform, glossy cubes of 'Cubi di Formaggio Dolce con Mela e Malto' are meticulously arranged on a pristine white Carrara marble slab. Each cube, approximately 3x3x3 cm, boasts a flawless, translucent amber malt syrup mirror glaze that catches the light. The underlying layers of pale cream Monterey Jack mousse, light golden dacquoise, and subtle amber apple gelee are subtly visible through the glaze's depth. Abundant negative space surrounds the precise arrangement. Each cube is crowned with a single, delicate curl of candied lemon peel or micro-shavings of fresh lemon zest, and accompanied by a tiny, vibrant green micro-mint sprig placed just beside it. The presentation is ultra-minimalist, showcasing the architectural precision and sophisticated simplicity of each petit four, set against a backdrop of dramatic professional lighting with soft, intentional shadows. An elegant Italian porcelain platter could also be used.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve chilled as a refined conclusion to a multi-course Italian fine dining experience.
Present on an elegant serving platter or tiered stand for communal enjoyment, characteristic of 'petit four' service in Italian patisseries.
Pair with a delicate espresso or a small glass of Moscato d'Asti.
instructions: Prepare Lemon-Malt Dacquoise: Preheat oven to 170°C. Whip egg whites to soft peaks. Gradually add 15g granulated sugar, whip to stiff peaks. Gently fold in almond flour, all-purpose flour, 7g malt syrup, and lemon zest. Spread mixture thinly (approx. 0.5 cm) onto a silicone mat or parchment-lined baking sheet. Bake 10-12 minutes until light golden. Cool completely. Cut into 3x3 cm squares.

Prepare Apple Liqueur Gelee: Bloom 1g gelatin sheet in ice water. Heat 30ml apple liqueur, 15ml water, 5g granulated sugar, and 4ml lemon juice until sugar dissolves. Squeeze excess water from gelatin; stir into hot liquid until dissolved. Pour gelee into a small, shallow container (approx. 0.5 cm deep). Chill until firm. Cut into 3x3 cm squares.

Prepare Monterey Jack Cream Mousse: Bloom 1g gelatin sheet in ice water. Gently heat 25g grated Monterey Jack cheese with 10ml of the heavy cream in a small saucepan until cheese melts into cream. Do not boil. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve into a bowl, discard solids. Squeeze excess water from gelatin; stir into warm cheese cream until dissolved. Let cool completely. In a separate bowl, whip remaining 50ml heavy cream with 8g granulated sugar and pinch of lemon zest to soft peaks. Gently fold cooled cheese cream mixture into whipped cream until just combined.

Assemble Cubes: Line small square silicone molds (approx. 3x3x3 cm) or a small rectangular mold. Place a dacquoise square at the bottom of each mold. Pipe or spoon Monterey Jack cream mousse over dacquoise, filling halfway. Place an apple liqueur gelee square on top of mousse. Top with more mousse, leveling the surface. Freeze cubes for at least 4 hours, or until completely solid.

Prepare Malt Syrup Mirror Glaze: Bloom 1.5g gelatin sheets in ice water. In a saucepan, combine 15ml water, 30g granulated sugar, and 15g malt syrup. Bring to a boil, then remove from heat. Add 20g chopped white chocolate and squeezed gelatin sheets. Stir until melted and smooth. Emulsify with an immersion blender, avoiding air bubbles. Strain glaze through a fine-mesh sieve. Cool glaze to 30-32°C.

Glaze and Garnish: Place frozen cubes on a wire rack set over a tray. Pour cooled mirror glaze evenly over each frozen cube, ensuring full coverage. Let excess glaze drip off. Carefully transfer glazed cubes to a serving platter using an offset spatula. Garnish each cube with a tiny, delicate curl of candied lemon peel or micro-shavings of fresh lemon zest and a single micro herb sprig.
notes: Ensure all components are thoroughly chilled or frozen before assembly and glazing for clean cuts and a perfect finish.
Achieving the correct glaze temperature (30-32°C) is crucial for a smooth, even coating.
Use high-quality Monterey Jack cheese for optimal flavor balance in the mousse.
traditional_techniques: Precise temperature control for glazes and mousses
Layering and assembly in molds for architectural desserts

recipes.recipe_name: Korean Braised Beef with Potatoes and Brown Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Korean Braised Beef with Potatoes and Brown Rice is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. Fluffy brown rice occupies one half of the bowl, neatly mounded. The other half features tender, rich brown beef chunks and golden-brown potato wedges, artfully arranged. The beef, cut into thick, irregular chunks, shows a glistening, tender texture. The potato wedges are soft and yielding, absorbing the deep brown braising liquid. A generous amount of the savory, glossy braising sauce is spooned over the beef and potatoes, creating a harmonious blend of colors and textures. The dish is garnished with vibrant green diagonal slices of fresh green onions and a sprinkle of light brown toasted sesame seeds, adding freshness and a subtle crunch. The background features a simple wooden table surface, a grey cotton napkin folded beside the bowl, and a set of traditional Korean chopsticks and a Korean spoon resting on the table. Natural, even light illuminates the dish, highlighting its rich colors and inviting textures. The overall presentation is clean, professional, and authentic to Korean culinary aesthetics.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with an assortment of traditional banchan (small side dishes) such as kimchi, pickled radish, or seasoned spinach.
Enjoy with a Korean-style spoon for the braising liquid and rice, and chopsticks for the beef and potatoes.
Often served as a comforting main course, especially during colder months.
instructions: Cut beef into 4-5 cm thick chunks. Pat dry.
Peel potato. Cut into large wedges or 3-4 cm thick pieces.
Peel and roughly chop onion.
Peel and mince garlic and ginger.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Brown beef chunks on all sides. Remove beef from pot. Set aside.
Add chopped onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic and ginger. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return beef to the pot.
In a separate bowl, whisk together soy sauce, mirin, sesame oil, sugar/honey, and gochujang (if using).
Pour sauce mixture and water/broth over beef. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and braise for 1.5 hours.
Add potato wedges to the pot. Continue to braise for another 30-40 minutes, or until beef is very tender and potatoes are cooked through.

While beef braises, cook brown rice according to package instructions. Typically, combine 250g brown rice with 500ml water in a pot. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 40-45 minutes until water is absorbed.
Slice green onions for garnish.
Taste braising liquid. Adjust seasoning if needed.
Serve braised beef and potatoes over cooked brown rice. Garnish with sliced green onions and toasted sesame seeds.
notes: For deeper flavor, you can marinate the beef in the sauce ingredients for at least 1 hour or overnight before browning and braising.
traditional_techniques: Layering of savory and sweet flavors

recipes.recipe_name: Apple Cinnamon Crumble
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of apple cinnamon crumble served in a small, round white ceramic ramekin. The topping features a rugged, golden-brown crust of toasted oats and butter clumps with visible granules of sugar. Deep amber apple juices bubble slightly around the inner rim of the dish. Inside, thick 2cm apple wedges are softened and coated in a dark cinnamon glaze. The ramekin sits on a weathered dark wood table. A simple stainless steel dessert spoon rests on a folded cream linen napkin next to the dish. Warm, soft kitchen lighting highlights the crunchy texture of the oats and the gentle steam rising from the center.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a dollop of thick clotted cream
Pour warm vanilla custard over the portion
Accompany with a scoop of vanilla bean ice cream
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Peel, core, and cut apples into 2cm wedges.
Toss apples with 50g sugar, 2g cinnamon, and lemon juice in a large bowl.
Transfer the apple mixture into a 20cm baking dish.
Combine flour, oats, remaining 50g sugar, and 3g cinnamon in a separate bowl.
Rub cold butter cubes into the flour mixture using fingertips.
Stop when the mixture forms coarse, pea-sized clumps.
Spread the oat crumble topping evenly over the apples.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until the topping is golden and crisp.
Cool for 10 minutes before serving to allow juices to thicken.
notes: Use tart apples to balance the sweetness of the sugar
Keep butter very cold to ensure a crumbly rather than greasy texture
Add a pinch of salt to the crumble topping to enhance the flavor

recipes.recipe_name: Beetroot Risotto with Seared Scallops
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of vibrant magenta beetroot risotto is artfully spooned onto a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, forming a natural, organic mound with moderate negative space. The risotto appears creamy and fluid, not stiff. Four plump, golden-brown seared sea scallops, with pearly white interiors visible, are placed elegantly on top of the risotto. A scattering of bright green chopped fresh flat-leaf parsley provides a vivid color contrast. A fresh lemon wedge rests beside the scallops. The plate is set on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, capturing the natural light of a modern bistro. A neatly folded white cotton napkin lies beside the plate. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a casual restaurant atmosphere, keeping the focus entirely on the dish.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Roast quartered beetroot for 30-40 minutes until tender. Let cool slightly. Purée roasted beetroot in a food processor until smooth. Set aside.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat. Add diced shallot. Sauté until softened, about 3 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice to the pot. Stir constantly for 2 minutes until rice edges become translucent.
Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed.
Stir in the beetroot purée until well combined.
Add one ladle of warm vegetable broth to the rice. Stir continuously until liquid is absorbed.

Continue adding broth, one ladle at a time, stirring constantly and waiting for each addition to be absorbed before adding the next. This process takes about 18-20 minutes. The risotto should be creamy and the rice tender but still have a slight bite (al dente).

Remove risotto from heat. Stir in cold butter cubes and grated Parmesan cheese. Stir vigorously for 1-2 minutes until butter and cheese are fully incorporated and risotto is creamy (mantecaura). Season with salt and pepper to taste. Cover and let rest for 2 minutes.
While risotto rests, heat remaining 15 ml olive oil in a large non-stick pan over high heat until shimmering. Season scallops generously with salt and pepper.
Place scallops in the hot pan without overcrowding. Sear for 2-3 minutes per side until a deep golden-brown crust forms and scallops are opaque through the center. Do not overcook.

Spoon a generous portion of creamy beetroot risotto onto the center of each white porcelain plate. Arrange 4 seared scallops on top of the risotto. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley and a lemon wedge. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Sun-Dried Tomato and Greens Risotto
recipes.visual_description: The creamy, golden risotto is served in a rustic, wide ceramic bowl, showing its fluid, unctuous consistency. Flecks of vibrant green from the tender, chopped broccoli rabe are interspersed with the deep, reddish-orange hues of thinly sliced sun-dried tomatoes and wilted spinach. A generous mound of freshly grated Parmesan cheese melts gently into the warm grains, creating delicate white streaks. A small swirl of bright green extra virgin olive oil glistens on top. The dish is placed on a well-worn wooden kitchen table, alongside a simple fork and spoon. A casually folded linen napkin and a small, plain water glass complete the homely, inviting scene under warm, ambient kitchen lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately in wide, shallow bowls.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
instructions: Heat vegetable broth in a saucepan. Keep it simmering on low heat.
Trim and chop broccoli rabe into 2 cm pieces. Blanch in boiling water for 2 minutes. Drain and set aside.
Drain sun-dried tomatoes and thinly slice.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add finely diced onion. Cook until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice to the pot. Stir constantly for 2 minutes until grains are slightly translucent at the edges.
If using, add white wine. Stir until completely absorbed.
Begin adding hot broth, one ladleful (about 125 ml) at a time. Stir continuously. Allow each ladleful to be almost fully absorbed before adding the next.
After about 10 minutes of adding broth, stir in the blanched broccoli rabe and sliced sun-dried tomatoes.
Continue adding broth and stirring. After approximately 18-20 minutes, when the rice is al dente (tender with a slight bite), stir in the fresh spinach. Cook until spinach wilts.
Remove from heat. Stir in 80 g of grated Parmesan cheese. Season with salt and black pepper to taste. The risotto should be creamy and fluid (all'onda).
Let risotto rest for 1 minute before serving.
notes: Stir risotto continuously for creamy texture.
Add broth gradually, allowing each addition to absorb.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Venison and Plum Stew
recipes.visual_description: A hearty individual portion of rustic venison and plum stew is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl, set on a simple light wooden table. Large, tender, irregular chunks of braised venison are nestled amongst rustic, 3 cm diced potato cubes, coarsely diced onions, and vibrant roughly chopped kale. Halved deep purple plums add a pop of color and subtle sweetness. The stew features a rich, glossy, deep reddish-brown sauce, thick enough to coat all ingredients. A single sprig of fresh thyme garnishes the top, adding a touch of green. The overall composition is professional yet approachable, with moderate negative space. A neatly folded cotton napkin rests beside the bowl. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and inviting warmth against a subtly blurred modern bistro background.

ingredients.name: Venison shoulder, trimmed and cut into 5 cm chunks
Potatoes (e.g., Yukon Gold), peeled and 3 cm diced
Kale, tough stems removed, roughly chopped

instructions: Preheat large stockpots over high heat. Add olive oil.
Working in batches, sear venison chunks until deeply browned on all sides. Remove venison from pots. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add onions, carrots, and celery to pots. Cook until softened, about 10-12 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Sprinkle flour over vegetables. Cook, stirring constantly, for 3 minutes to create a roux.
Gradually pour in red wine, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pots. Bring to a simmer.
Stir in beef broth and tomato paste. Return seared venison to the pots. Add thyme sprigs and bay leaves.
Bring stew to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 2-3 hours, or until venison is very tender.
Add diced potatoes and halved plums to the pots. Continue to simmer, uncovered, for 20-30 minutes, or until potatoes are tender.
Stir in chopped kale. Cook for 5-7 minutes, until kale is wilted and tender-crisp.
Remove bay leaves and thyme sprigs. Season stew generously with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve hot.

recipes.recipe_name: Orecchiette with Sausage and Broccoli Rabe
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Orecchiette with Sausage and Broccoli Rabe is served in a shallow white porcelain bowl. The little ear pasta is tossed with vibrant green, tender-crisp broccoli rabe florets and leaves. Large, 2cm rustic chunks of seared pork sausage are scattered throughout, showing a deep golden-brown crust from the pan. The pasta is coated in a glossy, translucent emulsion of olive oil, garlic, and starch. Fine shavings of Pecorino Romano cheese and small red chili flakes are sprinkled over the top. The bowl rests on a rustic dark wood table with a neutral linen napkin. Natural daylight emphasizes the contrast between the dark greens and the caramelized meat.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Altamura bread
Pair with a glass of Primitivo red wine
Drizzle with fresh raw olive oil at the table
instructions: Boil 4 liters of salted water in a large pot.
Remove sausage casings and break meat into 2cm chunks.
Heat olive oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat.
Brown sausage chunks for 6 minutes until golden and cooked through.
Remove sausage from pan and set aside, leaving the fat.
Add garlic and chili flakes to the pan. Sauté for 1 minute.
Trim broccoli rabe into 4cm pieces.
Cook orecchiette in the boiling water according to package directions.
Add broccoli rabe to the pasta water 4 minutes before the pasta is al dente.
Reserve 200ml of pasta water and drain the pasta and greens.
Add pasta, greens, and sausage chunks to the garlic oil.
Pour in 100ml of reserved water. Toss vigorously over high heat.
Remove from heat. Stir in Pecorino Romano until a glossy sauce forms.
notes: Use bronze-die pasta for better sauce adhesion
Ensure the sausage is browned well for maximum flavor
Do not overcook the broccoli rabe to maintain its bright green color

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Tuscan Chicken Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Creamy Tuscan Chicken Pasta is artfully plated on a round, clean white porcelain dinner plate. The creamy fettuccine, intertwined with golden-brown chicken chunks and vibrant green spinach, forms a neat mound in the center. Interspersed are deep red sun-dried tomato slices and earthy brown mushroom slices. The chicken chunks are irregularly shaped, about 2 cm, displaying a seared crust. A light drizzle of the creamy sauce coats the pasta, showing its rich texture. A sprinkle of freshly grated Parmesan cheese and finely chopped fresh basil leaves garnish the top, adding contrasting color and freshness. The arrangement is organic, allowing ingredients to show naturally. The plate is positioned on a simple light wooden table. A folded white cotton napkin and classic silver fork and spoon are placed beside the plate, with a small Italian-style bread roll. Natural, soft lighting highlights the textures and colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
Offer crusty Italian bread for dipping in the sauce.
Pair with a glass of dry white wine, like a Chianti Classico.

ingredients.name: Sun-dried tomatoes, oil-packed, drained and sliced

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken. Let rest. Cut into 2 cm chunks.
Add diced onion to the skillet. Sauté 3 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Sauté 5-7 minutes until mushrooms are tender and browned.
Stir in sun-dried tomatoes and red pepper flakes (if using). Cook 1 minute.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet.
Add heavy cream and grated Parmesan cheese. Stir until cheese is melted and sauce slightly thickens.
While sauce simmers, cook fettuccine according to package directions in salted water until al dente. Drain, reserving 120 ml pasta water.
Add fresh spinach to the sauce. Cook until wilted, about 1-2 minutes.
Add cooked pasta and chicken chunks to the sauce. Toss to combine. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water as needed.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
notes: For extra richness, add a knob of butter at the end.
Adjust red pepper flakes to desired spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Venison Loin with Plum Glaze and Potato Gratin
recipes.visual_description: A single, refined portion is presented on a clean, white round porcelain plate set on a simple light wooden table. The dish features thick, roasted venison chunks, a golden-brown square of potato gratin, and a vibrant green mound of sautéed kale. The venison, cooked to a medium-rare pink interior, shows a beautifully seared, deep brown crust. A glossy, dark ruby-red plum glaze is generously spooned over the venison, pooling slightly on the plate. The potato gratin exhibits distinct, thinly sliced potato layers within a creamy, golden-brown top. The kale is tender-crisp, displaying its natural deep green color. A small, fresh thyme sprig garnishes the plate. The composition is balanced with appropriate negative space. Standard silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin are placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors in a modern bistro setting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C for potato gratin.
Peel and thinly slice 21 kg potatoes.
Finely mince 1.5 kg onions and 26 garlic cloves.
In large pots, melt 500 g butter. Add minced onions and garlic. Sauté until translucent.
Pour in 10 L heavy cream. Bring to a simmer. Season with salt, pepper, and nutmeg.
Layer sliced potatoes in large baking dishes. Pour cream mixture over potatoes.
Bake for 45-60 minutes, or until golden and tender. Let cool slightly.
Pit and quarter 5.5 kg plums.
In large saucepans, melt 250 g butter. Add 2 kg chopped onions and remaining 26 minced garlic cloves. Sauté until soft.
Add quartered plums, 2 L red wine, 4 L beef stock, 500 mL balsamic vinegar, and 200 g brown sugar.
Bring to a boil. Reduce heat. Simmer for 30-40 minutes, stirring occasionally, until plums are very soft and liquid has reduced.
Strain mixture through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing solids to extract all liquid. Discard solids.
Return strained glaze to clean saucepans. Simmer gently until thickened to desired consistency. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
Preheat oven to 200°C for venison.
Trim any silver skin from 19 kg venison loins. Season venison generously with salt and pepper.
In large, heavy-bottomed pans, heat 1 L olive oil over high heat.
Sear venison loins on all sides until deeply browned, about 2-3 minutes per side.
Transfer seared venison to large roasting pans. Add fresh thyme and rosemary sprigs.
Roast in preheated oven for 15-25 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 54-57°C for medium-rare.
Remove venison from oven. Rest for 10-15 minutes before slicing.
Wash and trim 7.5 kg kale. Remove tough stems. Roughly chop leaves.
Blanch kale in large pots of boiling salted water for 2-3 minutes until tender-crisp.
Drain kale well. Immediately plunge into ice bath to stop cooking. Drain again thoroughly.
In large sauté pans, melt 250 g butter. Add 500 mL olive oil.
Add kale. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until heated through and tender. Season with salt and pepper.
Slice rested venison loins into thick chunks.
Cut potato gratin into individual square portions.
Place a portion of potato gratin on each plate.
Arrange 2-3 chunks of venison beside the gratin.
Place a mound of sautéed kale next to the venison.
Spoon plum glaze generously over venison.
Garnish with a small fresh thyme sprig.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Bell Pepper & King Oyster Mushroom Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Fermented Bell Pepper & King Oyster Mushroom Pasta is presented on a handcrafted, matte cream ceramic plate. The pasta, rigatoni, is generously coated in a vibrant, rustic orange-red sauce derived from blended fermented bell peppers, showing subtle flecks of green herbs. Scattered among the pasta are thick, seared King Oyster Mushroom discs, their surfaces a rich golden-brown with visible caramelization, providing a hearty, unsliced presence. The composition is natural and unforced, with ample white space on the plate. Fresh, roughly chopped parsley is sprinkled over the dish for a pop of green. The setting features a light, textured reclaimed wood table, an undyed linen napkin in beige, and soft, diffused natural light from the side. The background is clean and minimalist, allowing the dish to be the focal point.
instructions: Prepare fermented bell peppers: Wash 2 red bell peppers. Coarsely chop the peppers, including cores and seeds for zero-waste. Combine 500ml water and 10g sea salt to create a 2% brine. Submerge chopped peppers in the brine in a clean jar. Seal loosely. Let ferment at room temperature for 2-3 days until slightly tangy. Alternatively, use pre-fermented bell peppers.
Slice King Oyster Mushrooms: Cut each mushroom into thick discs, approximately 2cm thick. Season with salt and pepper.
Cook pasta: Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add pasta. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 250ml pasta cooking water. Drain pasta.
Sear mushrooms: Heat 30ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add mushroom discs. Sear 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and tender. Remove mushrooms from pan. Set aside.

Sauté aromatics: Dice remaining red bell pepper, red onion, and mince garlic. Add remaining 30ml olive oil to the same pan. Add diced bell pepper and onion. Sauté 5-7 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.

Create sauce: Add the fermented bell peppers and their brine to the pan with aromatics. Stir in nutritional yeast and vegetable broth. Bring to a simmer. Cook 5 minutes. Use an immersion blender to blend the sauce until mostly smooth but still with some texture. If too thick, add reserved pasta water.
Combine: Add cooked pasta to the sauce. Toss to coat evenly. Gently fold in the seared King Oyster Mushroom pieces.
Plate: Divide pasta among 4 plates. Garnish with fresh, roughly chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Cheesy Baked Latin Chicken and Rice Gratin
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Cheesy Baked Latin Chicken and Rice Gratin is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, centered on a simple wooden table. The gratin features a golden-brown, bubbly cheese and breadcrumb crust, with hints of vibrant green basil. Beneath the crust, tender chunks of seared chicken are visible, nestled within a rich, reddish-orange rice bed, colored by annatto and tomato. Colorful, cooked-through vegetables like orange butternut squash cubes, white potato pieces, green broccoli florets, and brown mushroom slices are interspersed throughout. The chicken pieces are whole, un-sliced chunks. The composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space on the plate. A folded white cotton napkin rests beside the plate. The scene is bathed in natural, even lighting, suggesting a relaxed, modern bistro atmosphere, with a subtly blurred background focusing solely on the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with a light vinaigrette.
Offer a side of your favorite hot sauce or a fresh salsa for added zest.

ingredients.name: Canned black beans, drained and rinsed
Shredded Monterey Jack or cheddar cheese

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Cut chicken thighs into 2-3 cm chunks. Toss chicken with Dijon mustard, 5 ml salt, and 2 ml black pepper.

Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides. Do not overcrowd. Cook in batches if necessary. Remove chicken and set aside.
Dice onion, red bell pepper, and carrot into 1 cm pieces. Mince jalapeño (remove seeds for less heat). Mince garlic.
Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to the same skillet. Sauté diced onion, bell pepper, and carrot for 5-7 minutes until softened. Add minced jalapeño and garlic. Cook for 2 minutes more until fragrant.
Stir in chili powder, annatto powder, smoked paprika, and dried oregano. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly, until aromatic.
Add rice to the skillet. Stir for 2 minutes to toast slightly.
Pour in beer, chicken broth, and diced tomatoes. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir in drained black beans and corn kernels.

Cut butternut squash, potato, and cremini mushrooms into 2-3 cm pieces. Cut broccoli into small florets. Toss all cut vegetables with 15 ml olive oil, 2 ml salt, and 1 ml black pepper on a baking sheet. Roast in the preheated oven for 15-20 minutes until tender-crisp.
Combine the partially cooked rice mixture, seared chicken chunks, and roasted vegetables in a large baking dish (or use the oven-safe skillet if large enough). Stir gently to combine.
Grate cheese. Roughly chop fresh basil leaves. In a small bowl, mix grated cheese, chopped basil, and panko breadcrumbs.
Sprinkle the cheese mixture evenly over the gratin in the baking dish.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until the gratin is bubbly and the cheese topping is golden brown and crispy.
Remove from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Adjust jalapeño quantity to your preferred spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Tatsoi Salad with Brown Butter Pecans, Cured Egg Yolk, and Aged Cheddar
recipes.visual_description: A meticulously composed individual salad portion rests on a pristine white bone china plate. Vibrant, dark green tatsoi leaves are artfully arranged in a natural, organic mound, occupying a precise area of the expansive white negative space. A few golden-brown, whole brown butter pecan halves are scattered artfully. A delicate dusting of bright orange, finely grated cured egg yolk adds a concentrated burst of color and unique texture. Ultra-thin, translucent curls of aged cheddar are delicately draped. A subtle sheen of clear lemon-mustard vinaigrette glistens on the leaves. The composition is bathed in dramatic, professional lighting, casting soft shadows. The plate sits on a luxurious white Carrara marble surface, with a crisply folded white linen napkin, maintaining an ultra-minimalist, elegant setting.
instructions: Prepare cured egg yolks: In a shallow dish, combine fine sea salt and granulated sugar. Create four small indentations in half of the mixture. Carefully place one egg yolk into each indentation. Gently cover yolks with the remaining salt-sugar mixture. Refrigerate for 12-24 hours.

Rinse cured egg yolks: Gently rinse each cured yolk under cold water to remove all salt-sugar mixture. Pat thoroughly dry with a paper towel. Dehydrate in a low oven at 60°C for 1-2 hours, or air dry until firm but still pliable. Once cooled, grate finely before serving.

Prepare brown butter pecans: Melt unsalted butter in a small saucepan over medium heat. Continue cooking until butter foams, then turns golden brown and smells nutty. Add pecan halves. Toast briefly for 1-2 minutes until fragrant. Season lightly with flaky sea salt. Transfer to a plate to cool.

Prepare lemon-mustard vinaigrette: In a small bowl, whisk together Dijon mustard, fresh lemon juice, a pinch of flaky sea salt, and freshly ground black pepper. Slowly drizzle in extra virgin olive oil while whisking continuously until the dressing is emulsified.
Assemble the salad: Gently wash and dry tatsoi leaves. In a mixing bowl, lightly toss the tatsoi leaves with a small amount of the prepared vinaigrette.

Plate: Divide the dressed tatsoi among four fine-dining plates, arranging it minimally in a natural, organic mound in the center. Artistically place a few brown butter pecan halves around the tatsoi. Grate a small amount of cured egg yolk over each salad. Using a vegetable peeler, shave ultra-thin curls of aged cheddar over the salad. Drizzle a small amount of additional vinaigrette around the plate for visual appeal. Serve immediately.
notes: Curing the egg yolks requires advance preparation, ideally overnight. They can be cured up to 2 days ahead and stored in the refrigerator.
Ensure tatsoi leaves are thoroughly dried to allow the dressing to adhere properly and maintain crispness.

recipes.recipe_name: Umami Garden Bites with Chicken Crackle
recipes.visual_description: A collection of individual, savory bites is artfully arranged on a light reclaimed wood board, showcasing a minimalist and ingredient-focused presentation. Each bite features a roasted mixed mushroom base, topped with finely diced pan-seared chicken and delicate flakes of white crab meat. A vibrant, plump fermented cherry tomato and a glossy, halved pickled cherry provide bursts of red and tartness. Irregular, golden-brown shards of crispy chicken crackle are placed atop for texture. A very small, thin piece of pale yellow American cheese is subtly tucked into each bite. The composition celebrates natural colors and textures, with ample white space around each element. The entire board is visible, not overcrowded. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the organic forms and simple beauty of the ingredients. An undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone is casually placed nearby, complementing the eco-conscious setting.
instructions: Prepare Fermented Cherry Tomatoes: Wash cherry tomatoes. Do not pierce. Dissolve 5g non-iodized salt in 250ml water to make brine. Place tomatoes in a clean jar. Pour brine over to cover. Seal jar with an airlock or loose lid. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days until slightly tangy. Refrigerate.

Prepare Quick Pickled Cherries: Halve and pit fresh cherries. In a small saucepan, combine white wine vinegar, 60ml water, sugar, and a pinch of salt. Bring to a simmer. Add cherries. Remove from heat immediately. Let cool completely in the liquid. Refrigerate.

Prepare Crispy Chicken Crackle: Carefully remove skin from chicken thighs. Place skin in a cold pan. Cook over low heat, rendering fat slowly, until skin is golden and very crisp. Drain crackle on paper towels. Season with a pinch of salt. Break into small, irregular pieces.

Cook Chicken and Mushrooms: Season chicken thigh meat with salt and pepper. Pan-sear chicken thighs until cooked through and internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Rest, then finely dice the cooked chicken meat. Clean mixed mushrooms. Slice larger mushrooms. Toss with olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast mushrooms at 200°C (390°F) for 15-20 minutes until tender and lightly browned.

Assemble Bites: Drain fermented tomatoes and pickled cherries. Flake fresh crab meat. Cut American cheese slices into very small, irregular pieces. On a serving board or individual small plates, arrange roasted mushrooms as a base. Top each mushroom with a small amount of diced chicken, a few flakes of crab meat, one fermented cherry tomato, one pickled cherry half, a shard of crispy chicken crackle, and a tiny piece of American cheese. Garnish generously with snipped fresh chives.

recipes.recipe_name: Bamboo Shoot and Cucumber Salad
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented in a clean, white ceramic bowl, showcasing a vibrant medley of textures and colors. Thinly sliced bamboo shoots, pale cream and slightly translucent, form the base. They are interspersed with bright green julienned cucumber and dark green rehydrated wakame. Slender strands of vibrant orange julienned carrot add a pop of color and visual interest. The light amber dressing lightly coats all components, giving them a subtle sheen. The arrangement is natural and organic, with ingredients artfully distributed and some strands of cucumber and wakame gently rising above the main mound. A scattering of white toasted sesame seeds and thinly sliced bright green scallion pieces are evenly distributed over the top as a fresh garnish. The bowl sits on a light-colored wooden table, accompanied by a pair of elegant wooden chopsticks and a folded white linen napkin beside it, suggesting a modern Japanese bistro setting. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its freshness and inviting textures. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space around the bowl.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately as a refreshing side dish.
Offer small individual portions as part of a multi-course Japanese meal.
Serve with steamed rice.
instructions: Rehydrate wakame in cold water for 5-10 minutes. Drain well. Gently squeeze out excess water. Chop into 2-3 cm pieces.
If using fresh bamboo shoots, blanch in boiling water for 5 minutes. Cool and slice thinly. If using canned, rinse thoroughly and slice thinly.
Julienne cucumber and carrot.
Combine sliced bamboo shoots, rehydrated wakame, julienned cucumber, and julienned carrot in a large mixing bowl.
Prepare the dressing: Whisk together soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, grated ginger, and sugar in a small bowl until sugar dissolves.
Pour dressing over the salad ingredients. Toss gently to coat all vegetables evenly.
Let the salad sit for 10-15 minutes to allow flavors to meld.
Divide salad among four serving bowls. Garnish each serving with thinly sliced green onion and toasted sesame seeds.

recipes.recipe_name: Cherry, Aged Cheddar, and Umami Textures
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of the deconstructed dessert is elegantly presented on a pristine white bone china plate. The composition is artistic and minimalist, featuring abundant negative space. A smooth, pale yellow quenelle of Aged Cheddar Cremeux rests slightly off-center. Vibrant ruby-red Cherry Fluid Gel is artfully swirled or dotted around the cremeux, creating dynamic color contrast. A thin, irregular, golden-brown shard of Savory-Sweet Potato Tuile stands upright, adding architectural height and textural intrigue. A delicate dusting of deep brown Caramelized Onion Dust is precisely placed, providing a subtle earthy tone. The plate is finished with a few glistening, almost translucent micro-droplets of the Chicken Consommé Glaze, imparting a refined sheen. The overall presentation is clean, organic, and sophisticated, emphasizing the purity of each component. The plate sits on a polished white Carrara marble surface, accented by a precisely folded crisp white linen napkin. Dramatic, soft professional lighting casts subtle shadows, highlighting the dessert's textures and contours.
instructions: For the Cherry Fluid Gel: Combine cherries, 100g sugar, and 100ml water in a saucepan. Simmer until cherries are soft. Blend until very smooth. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve. Whisk in agar-agar. Bring to a boil, simmer 1 minute. Pour into a shallow dish, chill until set. Re-blend the set gel until smooth and fluid. Keep refrigerated.

For the Aged Cheddar Cremeux: Grate cheddar cheese. Heat cream in a saucepan. In a bowl, whisk egg yolks with 50g sugar. Slowly temper hot cream into egg yolk mixture. Return to saucepan, cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until mixture thickens slightly (nappe consistency). Do not boil. Remove from heat, stir in grated cheddar until melted and smooth. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve. Chill thoroughly for at least 4 hours, or overnight.

For the Savory-Sweet Potato Tuile: Peel and dice potatoes. Boil until very tender. Drain well, rice or mash thoroughly until no lumps remain. Combine riced potato with melted butter, 50g sugar, roasted garlic powder, and plain flour. Mix into a smooth paste. Spread extremely thin onto a silicone mat or parchment paper using an offset spatula. Bake at 150°C (300°F) for 15-20 minutes, or until golden and crisp. Break into irregular shards. Store in an airtight container.

For the Caramelized Onion Dust: Slice onions thinly. In a heavy-bottomed pan, cook onions slowly over very low heat with a pinch of salt until deeply caramelized and brown, about 45-60 minutes. Add balsamic vinegar if desired, cook until evaporated. Spread caramelized onions thinly on a baking sheet. Dehydrate in an oven at 80°C (175°F) for 4-6 hours, or until completely brittle. Blend to a fine powder. Store in an airtight container.

For the Chicken Consommé Glaze: Roast chicken bones and mirepoix until deeply golden. Transfer to a large pot, cover with 2 liters cold water. Bring to a simmer, skim impurities. Simmer gently for 4 hours. Strain broth, discard solids. Chill broth. Skim all fat. Clarify broth: whisk egg whites into the cold broth, bring to a slow simmer, allowing raft to form. Gently ladle clear consommé through a cheesecloth-lined sieve. Reduce clarified consommé over medium heat until it becomes a syrupy glaze. Stir in 50g sugar and a pinch of salt. It should be sweet with a subtle savory depth. Keep warm for plating.

To Plate: Place a small quenelle or piped line of Cheddar Cremeux off-center on a white plate. Artfully drizzle or dot the Cherry Fluid Gel around the cremeux. Arrange one or two Potato Tuile shards vertically or at an angle. Dust a small amount of Caramelized Onion Dust nearby. Finish with a few micro-droplets or a thin line of the Chicken Consommé Glaze. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Beer-Braised Chicken with Fermented Carrot Relish
recipes.visual_description: A single, generously portioned braised chicken thigh, its skin a deep golden-brown, is centered on a natural, unglazed ceramic plate in an off-white tone. Beside the chicken, several substantial chunks of roasted carrot, tender and slightly caramelized, are artfully placed, showcasing their organic shapes. A small, vibrant mound of quick fermented carrot relish, with its thinly sliced orange carrots, red chili slivers, and green flecks, adds a bright contrast without being decorative. The plating is clean and minimalist, utilizing ample white space to highlight the pure beauty and natural textures of each ingredient. A few fresh basil leaves are loosely scattered on the chicken for a subtle green accent. The plate rests on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. An undyed linen napkin in a natural beige is folded simply to the side. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the dish, creating gentle shadows and emphasizing the organic forms. The background is uncluttered, hinting at natural elements like a subtle plant.
instructions: Prepare quick fermented carrot relish: Thinly slice 200g carrots. Mince 2 garlic cloves. Thinly slice 1 red chili. Combine carrots, garlic, chili in a bowl.
In a small pot, combine 250ml water, 5g sea salt, and 30ml white vinegar. Bring to a boil. Pour hot liquid over carrot mixture. Let cool completely. Refrigerate until ready to serve.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with sea salt and black pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken skin-side down until golden brown and crisp, 6-8 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 2 minutes. Remove chicken.
Add remaining 4 garlic cloves (sliced) and 2 red chilies (sliced) to the pot. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in lager beer. Scrape up any browned bits from the pot bottom. Bring to a simmer.
Cut remaining 300g carrots into 2cm chunks. Add to the pot. Return chicken to the pot, skin-side up. Pour in chicken stock. Liquid should come halfway up the chicken.
Bring to a gentle simmer. Cover pot. Transfer to a preheated oven at 170°C (340°F). Braise for 45-50 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C. Chicken should be tender.
Remove from oven. Stir in fresh basil leaves.
Serve braised chicken and carrots with a dollop of the quick carrot relish.
notes: Utilize chicken bones for homemade stock to minimize waste.
Compost all vegetable scraps.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Fermented Potato Puree and Chili Crisp
recipes.visual_description: A single, refined serving of Pan-Seared Chicken with Fermented Potato Puree and Chili Crisp is presented on a handcrafted, matte ceramic plate in a warm cream tone, resting on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. A generous, organic mound of creamy, off-white fermented potato puree sits slightly off-center, showcasing its smooth, natural texture. Beside it, a cluster of vibrant, bright green blanched green bean batons are artfully arranged, maintaining their crisp, elongated form. A single, pan-seared chicken thigh, with its deeply golden-brown, crispy skin facing upwards, is placed elegantly atop or beside the puree. The chicken is presented whole, not sliced.
